en: Thereafter, one should place the previously consecrated vases in a clockwise direction. Among them, having caused the *vijaya-kalaśa* of Akrūra to circumambulate the maṇḍala-circle, one should place it slightly to the south in the position facing the eastern gate of the maṇḍala, outside the circle of flames that constitutes the vajra-fence (*vajraprākāra*) and the rim of the world-system (*cakravāḍa*). On the left side, one should place the vases of Vairocana, Locanā, and the Sarvakarmika in due order, proceeding clockwise.

To the right [of the central deity] are Rūpavajrā and Dharmadhātuvajrāyamārī; to the left of the southern [deity] are Ratnasaṃbhava and Māmakī; to the right [of the southern deity] are Śabdavajrā and Prajñāntaka; to the left of the western [deity] are Amitābha and Pāṇḍarā; to the right [of the western deity] are Gandhavajrā and Padmāntaka; to the left of the northern [deity] are Amoghasiddhi and Tārā; and to the right [of the northern deity] are Rasavajrā, Sparśavajrā, and Vighnāntakī. Some maintain that the wrathful deities, such as Yamāri and the others, are located in the corners starting from the southeast.

Immediately after the Tathāgatas, the family mothers of the wrathful deities are placed on the right sides of the doors; this is another [view]. Following this, the placement in the other quarters should be inferred. There is also another opinion—what is the use of that? Thus is the placement of the vases in the Mañjuvajra maṇḍala.

Following that, the vases previously consecrated with the *adhivāsana* rite should be arranged in a clockwise direction. Among them, the *vijaya*-vase of the Wheel Lord (*cakreśvara*) should be carried around from the right side of the maṇḍala circle and placed slightly to the east of the gate of the maṇḍala, outside the perimeter of the vajra-enclosure and the ground of the blazing garland.

Finally, they should be placed on the right. On the left side, in their proper sequence and proceeding clockwise, are those of Vairocana, Locanā, and the all-activity vase; and on the right are those of Rūpavajrā, Dharmadhātuvajrī, and Yamāntaka.

To the left of the south are Ratnasambhava and Māmakī, and to the right are Ghoṣavajrā and Prajñāntakṛt. To the left of the west are Amitābha and Pāṇḍaravāsī, and to the right are Gandhavajrā and Padmāntakṛt. To the left of the north are Amoghasiddhi and Tārā, and to the right are Vajravārāhī.

[The seats] of Sparśavajrā and Vighnantaka are [in the intermediate directions]. According to some, the wrathful deities such as Yamāntaka and the others are in the intermediate directions starting from the southeast; according to others, immediately following all the Tathāgatas, the wrathful deities and the Family Mothers are in the right sides of the gates.

Following this, one should understand that the placement [of the vases] in other directions is also to be performed accordingly. Even though there may be other desires, what would be the use of them? Thus, this is the placement of the vases for the maṇḍala of Mañjuvajra.

In the Piṇḍīkrama maṇḍala, immediately after the Kula [deities] on the left, and first on the right, are the eight Bodhisattvas; in the corners are the Corner-Krodhas, with Yamāri following [the main deities], and Uṣṇīṣacakrin following [them]. Following Padmāntaka comes Sumbha—this is the distinction. According to this principle, the arrangement of the vases in other maṇḍalas is easy to understand, and thus it is not elaborated upon here.

In the mandala of the *Saṃpuṭatantra*, immediately to the left of the Family Mothers, and likewise first to the right, are the eight Bodhisattvas. In the corners are the wrathful deities; specifically, in the corners, following Yamāntaka is Uṣṇīṣacakravartin, and following Padmāntaka is Vighnāntaka. This is the distinction.
Following these [instructions], the arrangement of the vases for other mandalas is easy to understand and therefore has not been set forth here.
In the four corner vases, there are four arrows with feathers; they should be placed with the mantra *oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ*.

Furthermore, outside the Kālacakra dust maṇḍala, there are four vases in the cardinal directions beginning with the east; in the east is the fifth, the *jayakalaśa* (victory vase), and above that is the sixth, the *vijayakalaśa* (supreme victory vase) as a conch—this is according to the system of five jars. According to the system of ten jars, however, there are eight vases in the eight directions; the *vijayakalaśa* is located outside the western jar at a distance of two finger-breadths.

Outside the eastern jar, at a distance of two finger-breadths, is the Victory Jar (jayakalaśa); above that is the Great Victory Jar (mahāvijayakalaśa), and the conch is the eleventh. Thus it is also for jars numbering one hundred thousand; [this applies] to the rites of pacification, enrichment, and all ritual actions.

In the Kālacakra, outside of the colored powder maṇḍala, there are eight vases in the directions such as the east; outside of the western vase, at a distance of two finger-widths, is the Vijaya vase; and outside of the eastern vase, at a distance of two finger-widths, is the Jaya vase.

Above that, the conch-vessel of the Great Victorious Vase (Mahā-vaśitā-kalaśa) is the eleventh. To the east is the Victorious Vase (Jaya-kalaśa), which is the fifth. Above that, the Victorious Vase is the conch-vessel known as "Fierce" (Raudra); this refers to the position of the fifth vase. Regarding the positions of the ten vases, there are eight vases in the eight directions.

Two finger-breadths outside the western vase is the *vijaya* (victory) vase; two finger-breadths outside the eastern vase is the *vijaya* vase; and above that, the eleventh is the great *vijaya* conch-vessel (*mahā-vijaya-śaṅkha-dharmagaḍa*).
Likewise, among the hundreds of thousands of vases, the Great Victorious One (Mahā-vijaya) is the conch-shell; this applies to the peaceful, the increasing, and the all-accomplishing [rites] as well.
This is the procedure for the ritual placement (*kalaśanyāsa*).
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the placement of the vase.
